blocks.1: Legend says that when King Olav was to baptise the people at the Gulating, the men of Sogn were so stubborn that they kicked the basin out of Bishop Grimkjell's hands. The king would have none of this, so he had a baptismal font carved out of stone. The stone is shaped like a cube with sides of about 60 cm and a hollow cut into the top. This font they could not kick away. It was later placed in the church, where it still stands and is used as a font to this day.
blocks.2: It is this, and other legends, traditions and things that have happened in our village, that I want to share with you, if you find it worth the trouble to read on through this website. Many people have urged me to write down what I have heard, and otherwise learned, about Eivindvik, and that is what I have tried to do here.
blocks.4: Eivindvik seen from Fonnøya in 1938. Photo: Unknown.
blocks.5: I have probably written a little briefly about many things, perhaps in telegram style here and there, but that is in order to gather, in broad outline, as much as possible of what I have read and been told about the place, and at the same time to include something about more recent events that those of us who live here now have experienced ourselves. I cannot vouch that the material is historically correct, but I have made a point of including only things for which I can point to sources. I have also included a few of my prologues and verses.

blocks.8: You quiet, sheltered Eivindvik, you village by sound and bay, you make us all glad and rich, – the fairest we have seen. The area around the church in 2000, seen from Fonnevika. Photo: Knut Laasbye.
